chapter_theme: The three kinds of implication (இலக்கணாத் திரயம்), the Vedantic modes by which a word points beyond its literal sense, are placed in the states of the soul, and what lies beyond all implication is one's own true form; the senses fall like elephants to a well-aimed arrow.

2566.reading: Implication that leaves the literal sense goes into the void; implication that touches it without leaving gathers in the stilled state; implication that both leaves and keeps reaches as far as sat and the rest; what is pointed to beyond implication is the true form.
2566.nuance: விட்ட இலக்கணை, விடாத இலக்கணை and விட்டுவிடாத இலக்கணை are taken as the three lakshanas of Vedantic exegesis (jahat, ajahat and jahad-ajahat). வியோமம் (space, void), உபசாந்தம் (the stilled state) and சத்தாதி are taken as stages of the soul's ascent; where each mode is placed is the verse's own scheme and is not clear to me. இலக்கணாதீதம் சொரூபம் is the true form beyond them all.

2567.reading: When the arrow, fitted to the string and driven by the bow, struck its mark, the five killing elephants fell with the shaft; for the one who sits in the bow and shoots keenly, the light rises to meet him like a jewel set in stone.
2567.nuance: The five elephants are traditionally the five senses, and the arrow the aimed mind or the mantra; the reading is symbolic throughout. கல்கலன் என்னக் கதிர் எதிர் ஆமே is obscure: கல்கலன் may be a jewel of stone or a stone vessel. How the verse bears on the three implications is not stated.

links.note: 2566 names the third mode, implication that leaves and keeps (விட்டுவிடாத இலக்கணை); 2570 applies it to the great saying, as in the Vedantic example 'this is that Devadatta', to make the soul the Supreme.

2567: when the aimed arrow struck, the five killing elephants (கொல்லுங் களிறு ஐந்தும்) fell. Kural 24: one who guards the five (ஓரைந்தும்) with the goad (தோட்டி) of firmness is a seed for heaven. Both treat the five senses as elephants; the Kural controls them with a goad, Tirumular's aimed arrow fells them.
